description.value: The study examined how the emotional salience of graphic cigarette warning labels affects smokers' brain activity, recognition memory, and cigarette craving using fMRI.

value: the greater emotional response evoked by High ER labels will facilitate the processing of the information they contain; this will be reflected in greater activation of the amygdala, hippocampus and insula and result in better recognition and greater acute reduction in cigarette craving compared to the Low ER labels.

source_definition.value: Three stimulus conditions: HIGH (High emotional-reaction graphic warning labels), LOW (Low emotional-reaction graphic warning labels), and CONTROL (scrambled graphic warning labels).

spans.text: Graphic labels fMRI task: The labels were presented in a block design paradigm 36 with six different blocks for each of three stimulus types: HIGH (ie, High ER graphic warning labels), LOW (ie, Low ER graphic warning labels) and CONTROL (ie, scrambled graphic warning labels).

model_settings.value: Participant-level voxel-wise analyses used FILM (FMRIB's Improved General Linear Model) with local autocorrelation correction; three condition events were modeled with a double-b3 haemodynamic response function; group-level participant contrast maps were entered into single-group t tests; maps were thresholded at voxel-level z=2.3 and cluster-corrected at p<0.05 using family-wise error correction based on Gaussian Random Field theory.

description.value: Standard fMRI preprocessing and spatial normalization using FSL FEAT.

spans.text: Single-participant preprocessing included removal of regions outside the brain using brain extraction tool, 41 slice time correction, motion correction to the median image using the Motion Correction version of FMRIB's line image registration tool (MCFLIRT), 42 high-pass temporal filtering with a cut-off of 50s, spatial smoothing using a Gaussian kernel (5 mm full-width at half-maximum, isotropic) and mean based intensity normalization of all volumes using the same multiplicative factor.
